name: tabular-invalid-duplicate-column-name
description: A column name appears more than once in the first line (the column names) of a tabular file (reason a). The error does not depend on whether the repeated column is annotated: a repeated HED column, a repeated column with no annotation, a name repeated three times, and a repeated column that a sidecar annotates all fail. Distinct names pass, including a name that is a prefix of another (trial and trial_type). Names are compared exactly as written: a double quote is an ordinary character, so trial and "trial" are two names, and 1 and 1.0 are two names, not one number.
common_causes: A column copied when the table was exported or merged, keeping its name
Two tables joined side by side without renaming the columns they share
A tool that appends one column per annotation writing a column whose name already exists
Editing the header line by hand
explanation: The first line of a tabular file lists its column names, and each name may appear only once. When a name repeats, a sidecar entry or a curly-brace reference cannot say which of the columns it means, and assembling a row's annotation would combine the annotations of the repeated columns or lose one of them. Validators report this as TABULAR_INVALID before any row annotation is assembled; earlier validators reported such files as TAG_EXPRESSION_REPEATED, or not at all.
correction_strategy: Rename or remove the repeated column so that every column name in the header is unique, then give the renamed column its own sidecar entry if it carries information that should be annotated.

correction_examples.explanation: Renamed the second trial column after what it records
Merged the two HED columns into one, joining each row's two annotations with a comma

correction_patterns: Make every name in the header line unique
Rename a copied column after the information it holds
Keep one HED column per table
fix_instructions: 1. Read the header line of the tabular file and list the names that occur more than once
2. Decide for each repeated column whether it is a copy (remove it) or holds other information (rename it)
3. Add a sidecar entry for a renamed column if it should be annotated
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Compare the number of column names with the number of distinct column names
Column names that differ only by a suffix (trial, trial_type) are distinct

name: tabular-invalid-column-name-whitespace
description: A column name in the first line of a tabular file begins or ends with whitespace (reason b). A trailing or leading blank fails, on the HED column or on any other column, a padded name that is also repeated is reported under (b), trial beside a padded trial is one padded name rather than a repeat, and a name made only of a blank is padded and fails under (b), not as a blank name (c). A header naming trial for a sidecar entry trial fails when the header cell is padded. The same tables with unpadded names pass, including a name with an internal blank and a name that ends with a no-break space (U+00A0), which is not whitespace for this rule.
common_causes: A blank typed after a column name when the header line was edited by hand
A spreadsheet export that keeps a trailing blank from the source cell
Columns aligned with blanks for readability before the file was saved as TSV
A script that writes the header with a separator such as ', ' instead of a single tab
explanation: Each column name in the header must be exactly the name that sidecar entries and curly-brace references use. A name with leading or trailing whitespace (blank, tab, line feed, or carriage return) looks identical to the unpadded name but is a different string, so one validator would trim it and match a sidecar entry while another would not. The specification therefore makes the padding itself an error, TABULAR_INVALID, reported before any row annotation is assembled.
correction_strategy: Remove the leading and trailing whitespace from every column name in the header line, so that each name matches its sidecar entry exactly.

correction_examples.explanation: Removed the trailing blank so the column matches the sidecar entry trial
Removed the leading blank so the column is recognized as the HED column

correction_patterns: Trim leading and trailing whitespace from every header cell
Separate header cells with exactly one tab and nothing else
fix_instructions: 1. Open the tabular file in a plain-text editor that shows whitespace
2. Find header cells with blanks before or after the name
3. Remove the blanks, keeping exactly one tab between names
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Compare each header cell with its trimmed form
Blanks inside a name (trial type) are not padding and are not this error
A name made only of whitespace is padding, reason (b), not a blank name, reason (c)

name: tabular-invalid-blank-column-name
description: A column name in the first line of a tabular file is blank, the empty string (reason c). A first line that ends with a tab has a blank last name, a first line that is only a tab has two blank names, a blank name between two others fails, and two blank names are reported under (c) for each blank name, not as a repeated name under (a). A header naming trial for a sidecar entry trial fails when the header also has a blank column. The same tables without the blank column pass. An empty first line is a single blank column name, so a file whose first line is empty fails under this reason (its later lines also have two cells against one, reason f); either way the error is TABULAR_INVALID.
common_causes: A tab typed after the last column name when the header line was edited by hand
A spreadsheet export that writes an empty header cell for an unused or deleted column
Two tabs typed between column names where one was intended
A script that writes the header with a trailing separator after the last name
explanation: Every column of a tabular file needs a name, because sidecar entries and curly-brace references find a column by its name. An empty header cell gives its column no name at all: no sidecar entry can describe it, and a line that ends with a tab silently adds such a column. The specification therefore makes a blank column name an error, TABULAR_INVALID, reported once for each blank name by its column position before any row annotation is assembled. Several blank names are not a repeated name; each is reported as blank.
correction_strategy: Give every column in the header line a name, or remove the empty column (its header cell and the matching cell in every row), including any trailing tab at the end of the lines.

correction_examples.wrong: Header: onset, duration, HED, '' (the line ends with a tab)
correction_examples.explanation: Removed the trailing tab from the header and the rows, so the file has no unnamed last column

correction_examples.wrong: Header: onset, '', HED (blank name in the middle)
correction_examples.explanation: Named the empty column duration so that every column has a name

correction_patterns: Give every header cell a non-empty name
Remove trailing tabs from the header line and from every row
fix_instructions: 1. Open the tabular file in a plain-text editor that shows tabs
2. Find empty header cells, including one after a tab at the end of the header line
3. Name each empty column, or delete it from the header and from every row
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Check each header cell for the empty string, including the cell after a trailing tab
A name made only of whitespace is padding, reason (b), not a blank name
Several blank names are each reported as blank, not as a repeated name

name: tabular-invalid-value-whitespace
description: A value in a column with categorical or value HED annotations begins or ends with whitespace (reason d). In a categorical column, go with a trailing or leading blank, a value made only of a blank, and n/a with a trailing blank fail; in a value column, 30 with a trailing or leading blank fails. The same tables pass with go, 30, n/a, and an empty cell, and also with a HED column cell that has blanks around its tag, a categorical value ending with a no-break space (U+00A0, not whitespace for the rule; it only lacks an annotation, a warning), and a padded value in a column with no HED annotation. In a table with one annotated column, a line of only a blank is such a value (reason d), not a wrong cell count (reason f).
common_causes: A blank typed after a value when the table was edited by hand
A spreadsheet export that keeps a trailing blank from the source cell
Values aligned with blanks for readability before the file was saved as TSV
A script that writes n/a or a number with a separator such as ', ' instead of a single tab
explanation: Values are used exactly as written. A categorical value is matched to the keys of its sidecar annotation only when the two strings are identical, and a value-column value is substituted for the # of its template as written. A padded value looks the same as the unpadded one but matches no key, so its annotation would be lost with at most a missing-key warning, or it would carry its whitespace into the HED string. The specification therefore makes the padding itself an error, TABULAR_INVALID, reported column by column before the values are checked against their annotations and before any row annotation is assembled.
correction_strategy: Remove the leading and trailing whitespace from every value in the columns that the sidecar annotates, so that each categorical value matches its sidecar key exactly and each value-column value is a clean value.

correction_examples.wrong: trial column value 'go ' (trailing blank) with sidecar key go
correction_examples.explanation: Removed the trailing blank so the value matches the sidecar key go
Removed the trailing blank so the value is read as a missing value

correction_examples.wrong: age column value ' 30' (leading blank) with sidecar template Age/#
correction_examples.explanation: Removed the leading blank so Age/30 is substituted

correction_patterns: Trim leading and trailing whitespace from every value in annotated columns
Separate cells with exactly one tab and nothing else
fix_instructions: 1. Find the columns that the sidecar annotates with HED (categorical and value entries)
2. Look for values with blanks before or after them, including a value of only blanks and n/a with a blank
3. Remove the blanks, keeping exactly one tab between cells
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Compare each value in an annotated column with its trimmed form
Blanks inside a value (go now) are not padding and are not this error
An empty cell and n/a are missing values; a cell of only blanks and n/a with a blank are padding
The HED column and columns with no HED annotation are not checked
A no-break space is not whitespace for this rule

name: tabular-invalid-empty-line
description: A line other than the first of a tabular file is empty, with no characters before its line terminator (reason e). An empty line between two rows fails, and so does an empty last line, which two line endings at the end of the file make; a single line ending at the end of the file is not an empty line. An empty line is reported as an empty line only, not also as a wrong cell count (reason f), and an empty first line is a blank column name (reason c), not this error. The same tables without the empty line pass.
common_causes: A blank line left between rows when the file was edited by hand
An extra line ending at the end of the file, such as one added by an editor or by a script that writes a line ending after every row and then another
Rows from two files pasted together with a blank line between them
A script that writes an empty row for a record it has no data for
explanation: Every line after the first is a row of the table, so an empty line is a row with no cells at all, not a row of missing values. The specification therefore makes an empty line an error, TABULAR_INVALID, reported for every offending line by its line number (the column-name line is line 1) before any row annotation is assembled, and the rows of the file are then not validated. A file may end with a single line ending; two line endings at the end make an empty last line.
correction_strategy: Delete each empty line. If the line was meant to be a row of missing values, write n/a in each cell. End the file with one line ending, not two.

correction_examples.explanation: Deleted the empty line between the rows

correction_examples.wrong: File ends 'b<TAB>Blue' followed by two line endings
correction_examples.correct: File ends 'b<TAB>Blue' followed by one line ending
correction_examples.explanation: Removed the extra line ending so there is no empty last line

correction_examples.wrong: Empty line meant as a row with no values in a two-column table
correction_examples.explanation: Wrote the missing values explicitly so the row has as many cells as the header

correction_patterns: End the file with exactly one line ending
Write a row of missing values with n/a in each cell
fix_instructions: 1. Open the tabular file in a plain-text editor that shows line endings
2. Find lines with nothing on them, including a second empty line at the end of the file
3. Delete them, or replace one that stands for a row with n/a in each cell
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Check every line after the first for zero characters before the line terminator
One line ending at the end of the file is allowed; two make an empty last line
An empty first line is a blank column name (reason c), not an empty line
A line of only tabs with the right number of cells, or of only blanks, is not empty
The reported line number counts the column-name line as line 1

name: tabular-invalid-cell-count
description: A line other than the first of a tabular file has a different number of tab-separated cells than the first line (reason f). In a two-column table, a row one cell short, a first data row one cell long, a later row one cell long, a line of only a blank (one cell), and a line of only tabs with three cells fail; in a combined sidecar and table test a short row fails. A line of only tabs with as many cells as the first line is a row of missing values and passes, and so does a blank-only line in a table with one column and no HED annotations (a whitespace value that is not annotated). An empty line is reported as an empty line (reason e) only, not under this error.
common_causes: A cell dropped from a row when the file was edited by hand, so that the row has too few tabs
A value that contains a tab, which splits it into two cells
A row written by a script that omits trailing empty cells
Spaces typed in place of tabs between values, which merges two cells into one
explanation: The cells of a row are matched to the column names by position, so a row with a different number of cells than the header cannot be assigned to its columns reliably: a missing cell shifts or loses a value, and an extra cell has no column. Tools that read such a file may pad the short row or drop the extra cell without saying so, which hides the problem. The specification therefore makes it an error, TABULAR_INVALID, reported for every offending line by its line number (the column-name line is line 1), with the number of cells in the line and the number expected, before any row annotation is assembled; the rows of the file are then not validated.
correction_strategy: Give every row as many tab-separated cells as the header line. Write an empty cell as n/a or as nothing between two tabs; never drop it. Remove an extra cell, or add a column name for it, and replace a tab inside a value.

correction_examples.correct: Row 'b<TAB>Blue', or 'b<TAB>n/a' when there is no HED value
correction_examples.explanation: Added the missing cell so the row has two cells like the header

correction_examples.correct: Row 'b<TAB>Blue', or add a third column name to the header and a cell to every row
correction_examples.explanation: Removed the extra cell, or gave it a column so all rows match

correction_examples.wrong: Header response<TAB>HED; a line holding only a blank
correction_examples.explanation: A line of only a blank has one cell; a row of missing values needs a cell for each column

correction_patterns: Count the tabs in each row against the header
Write empty cells as n/a or as nothing between tabs, never omit them
fix_instructions: 1. Open the tabular file in a plain-text editor that shows tabs
2. Count the cells in the header line, then in each following line
3. Add the missing cells (n/a if there is no value) or remove the extra ones
4. Validate the file again
validation_hints: Compare the number of tab-separated cells of every line after the first with the first line
A line of only tabs with as many cells as the header is a row of missing values
A line of only blanks has one cell: wrong count unless the table has one column
An empty line is reported as an empty line (reason e), not as a wrong count
The error gives the line number, the cells found, and the cells expected
